"'''USS ''Callister'''''" is the first episode of the fourth series of the anthology programme ''[[Black Mirror]]''. Written by series creator [[Charlie Brooker]] and William Bridges and directed by [[Toby Haynes]], it first aired on [[Netflix]], along with the rest of season four, on 29 December 2017.

The episode follows Robert Daly ([[Jesse Plemons]]), a reclusive but gifted programmer and co-founder of a popular immersive [[virtual reality]]-based [[massively multiplayer online game]] who is bitter over the lack of recognition of his position from his coworkers. He takes out his frustrations by simulating a ''[[Star Trek]]''–like space adventure within the game, using his co-workers' DNA to create sapient digital clones of them. Acting as the captain of the USS ''Callister'' starship, Daly is able to order his co-workers around, bend them to his will, and mistreat them if they get out of line. When Daly brings newly hired Nanette Cole ([[Cristin Milioti]]) into his game, she encourages the other clones to revolt against Daly.

In contrast to most ''Black Mirror'' episodes, "USS ''Callister''" contains overt comedy, and it has many special effects. As a fan of ''Star Trek'', Bridges was keen to introduce many details from the show into "USS ''Callister''", though the episode was conceived mostly with ''[[The Twilight Zone (1959 TV series)|The Twilight Zone]]''{{'}}s 1961 episode "[[It's a Good Life (The Twilight Zone)|It's a Good Life]]" and the ''[[Viz (comics)|Viz]]'' character [[Playtime Fontayne]] in mind. The episode's reception was overwhelmingly positive, with reviewers praising the allusions to ''Star Trek'', the acting, and the cinematography. Some critics saw the episode as being about <!-- this is what critics have said - see Analysis -->male abuse of authority, and compared Daly to contemporary events surrounding internet bullies and [[Harvey Weinstein sexual abuse cases|sexual abuse committed by Harvey Weinstein]]. In 2018, the episode won four [[Primetime Emmy Award]]s, including [[Primetime Emmy Award for Outstanding Television Movie|Outstanding Television Movie]] and [[Primetime Emmy Award for Outstanding Writing for a Limited Series, Movie, or Dramatic Special|Outstanding Writing for a Limited Series, Movie, or Dramatic Special]], and was nominated for three other Emmy Awards. A sequel episode, titled "[[USS Callister: Into Infinity|USS ''Callister''{{hairsp}}: Into Infinity]]", was released as part of the seventh series of ''Black Mirror'', making it the only episode to receive a sequel.

== Plot ==
Aboard the spaceship USS ''Callister'', Captain Robert Daly ([[Jesse Plemons]]) and his crew destroy their arch-enemy Valdack's ([[Billy Magnussen]]) ship, but he escapes. The crew celebrates, with Daly kissing both female crewmates.

The real-life version of Daly is [[chief technical officer|CTO]] at Callister Inc. The company was co-founded by Daly and James Walton ([[Jimmi Simpson]]), the company's [[chief executive officer|CEO]], which produces the immersive [[virtual reality]]-based [[massively multiplayer online game]] ''Infinity'', in which users control a starship in a simulated reality. Daly is treated poorly by his fellow employees, who appear identical to Captain Daly's crewmates.

New programmer Nanette Cole ([[Cristin Milioti]]) praises Daly's work on ''Infinity'', but the more assertive Walton interrupts to show her around the office. When Daly returns home, he opens a development build of ''Infinity'' which is [[Video game modding|modded]] to resemble his favourite television show ''Space Fleet''. As Captain Daly, he berates the crewmates, strangling a subservient "Lieutenant" Walton.

After employee Shania Lowry ([[Michaela Coel]]) warns Nanette to beware of Daly, he takes a discarded coffee cup of Nanette's and uses her DNA to replicate her consciousness within his development build. As "Lieutenant Cole", Nanette finds herself aboard the USS ''Callister'', where "Lieutenant" Lowry explains that they are [[Virtual actor|digital clones]] of Callister Inc. staff members. Confused and distraught, Nanette attempts to escape the ship but is teleported back to the bridge. She refuses to obey Daly's commands, so he removes her facial features, suffocating her, until she relents.

The crew embark on a mission in which they apprehend Valdack but spare his life. After Daly leaves, Nanette finds a way to send a game invitation containing a message for help to the real-world Nanette. When the real-world Nanette asks the real-world Daly about the message, he dismisses it as [[Spamming|spam]]. Daly enters the game to interrogate his crew and transforms Lowry into a monster when she defends Nanette. Once Daly departs, Nanette identifies a distant wormhole as an [[uplink]] to ''Infinity''{{'}}s next update; she surmises that by flying into the wormhole, they will be deleted and therefore die. Walton is very hesitant to help; he explains that Daly has previously recreated his son Tommy within the game, throwing him out of an airlock to punish Walton. He also points out that since Daly still has all their DNA, he can just recreate them and punish them further. Nanette promises the crew that they will recover the lollipop containing Tommy's DNA.

When Daly returns, Nanette persuades him to take her on a mission to Skillane IV alone. She strips to her bathing suit and runs into a nearby lake, enticing a reluctant Daly to swim with her. He leaves behind the omnicorder, which allows him to control the game, on the shore. The crew teleports the omnicorder onto their ship and uses it to access sexually explicit images of Nanette on her PhotoCloud account, which they then use to blackmail the real-life Nanette into ordering a pizza at Daly's apartment and stealing his DNA samples while he answers the door. The cloned crew then teleport digital Nanette onto the ship.

As Daly resumes play, he discovers the crew are escaping. He commandeers a crashed spaceship to pursue them through an asteroid belt. The ''Callister'' collides with an asteroid; Walton repairs the thrusters manually, incinerating himself, and the ship accelerates into the wormhole. The firewall detects Daly's modded build and locks his controls, rendering him physically unable to exit the game as it is deleted around him. In the real world, Daly is left sitting motionless, implying he has died from the side effect.

The crew reawakens in the un-modded version of ''Infinity'' with Plowman and Lowry restored to human form. Now free, they continue their adventure, with Nanette leading them, after interacting with an annoyed user, "Gamer691" ([[Aaron Paul]]).

==Production==
Whilst series one and two of ''Black Mirror'' were shown on [[Channel 4]] in the UK, Netflix commissioned the series for 12 episodes (split into two series of six episodes) in September 2015 with a bid of $40 million,<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Birnbaum |first=Debra |date=25 September 2015 |title='Black Mirror' Lands at Netflix |url=https://variety.com/2015/digital/news/netflix-black-mirror-new-episodes-1201602037/ |journal=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]] |access-date=25 July 2018}}</ref><ref name="guardian commission" /> and in March 2016, Netflix outbid Channel 4 for the right to distribute the series in the UK.<ref name="guardian commission">{{Cite news |last=Plunkett |first=John |date=29 March 2016 |title=Netflix deals Channel 4 knockout blow over Charlie Brooker's Black Mirror |url=https://www.theguardian.com/media/2016/mar/29/netflix-channel-4-charlie-brooker-black-mirror |work=[[The Guardian]]}}</ref> The six episodes in series four were released on Netflix simultaneously on 29 December 2017.<ref name="RT interview" /> "USS ''Callister''" is listed as the first episode, though as each episode is standalone the episodes can be watched in any order.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Thomas |first=Leah |date=29 December 2017 |title=Watch The 'Black Mirror' Season 4 Episodes In This Order For The Best Viewing Experience |url=https://www.bustle.com/p/watch-the-black-mirror-season-4-episodes-in-this-order-for-the-best-viewing-experience-7690945 |access-date=2 September 2018 |website=[[Bustle (magazine)|Bustle]]}}</ref>

===Conception and writing===
{{Quote box|quote=Sometimes ideas come about where we say, "What haven't we done yet," and we said, "We haven't done space, and what's a 'Black Mirror' version of a space epic?"|align=right|width=30%|author=[[Charlie Brooker]]|source=interview with ''[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]]''<ref name="Variety interview" />}}
The episode was written in November 2016<ref name="ew interview">{{Cite magazine |last=Hibberd |first=James |date=29 December 2017 |title=''Black Mirror'': Here's the secret inspiration for 'USS Callister' |url=https://ew.com/tv/2017/12/29/black-mirror-u-s-s-callister-interview/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171229164415/http://ew.com/tv/2017/12/29/black-mirror-u-s-s-callister-interview/ |archive-date=29 December 2017 |access-date=29 December 2017 |magazine=[[Entertainment Weekly]]}}</ref> by series creator [[Charlie Brooker]] along with William Bridges, who previously co-wrote series 3 episode "[[Shut Up and Dance (Black Mirror)|Shut Up and Dance]]".<ref name="RT interview">{{Cite web |last=Ling |first=Thomas |date=7 December 2017 |title=Black Mirror season 4 episode guide: Charlie Brooker reveals new plot and episode details |url=http://www.radiotimes.com/news/on-demand/2017-12-07/black-mirror-season-4-netflix-episode-guide/ |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171210155309/http://www.radiotimes.com/news/on-demand/2017-12-07/black-mirror-season-4-netflix-episode-guide/ |archive-date=10 December 2017 |access-date=2 September 2018 |website=[[Radio Times]]}}</ref> Brooker said that the episode was based around doing "a 'Black Mirror' version of a space epic",<ref name="Variety interview">{{Cite web |last=Clarke |first=Stewart |date=6 December 2017 |title=Charlie Brooker Talks 'Black Mirror' Season 4, Heading to Space, and Outflanking Reality |url=https://variety.com/2017/tv/news/charlie-brooker-black-mirror-1202631889/ |access-date=10 December 2017 |website=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]]}}</ref> an idea that began during the filming of series three episode "[[Playtest (Black Mirror)|Playtest]]".<ref name="dog interview" /> Inspired partially by "[[It's a Good Life (The Twilight Zone)|It's a Good Life]]",<ref name="ew interview" /> a 1961 episode of ''[[The Twilight Zone (1959 TV series)|The Twilight Zone]]'' about a boy with "God-like powers", and partially by ''[[Viz (comics)|Viz]]'' character Playtime Fontayne, an adult who makes people participate in childish games, Charlie Brooker compares Daly to dictator [[Kim Jong-un]] and to "someone going online and venting".<ref name="ds interview" /> Brooker said that they also at times called the episode an "adult ''[[Toy Story]]''", making the comparison between the toys in Andy's room having to hold still until Andy leaves, and the virtual crew having to hold back their true thoughts until Daly left the simulation.<ref name="thr aug2018">{{Cite web |last=Huff |first=Lauren |date=3 August 2018 |title='Black Mirror' Showrunners Reveal Surprising Link Between 'Toy Story' and "USS Callister" |url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/news/black-mirror-showrunners-talk-surprising-toy-story-uss-callister-link-1130672 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180803190324/https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/news/black-mirror-showrunners-talk-surprising-toy-story-uss-callister-link-1130672 |archive-date=3 August 2018 |access-date=3 August 2018 |website=[[The Hollywood Reporter]]}}</ref> Though sometimes very bleak, the episode has comedy that may be considered atypical for the show,<ref name="RT interview" /> and Brooker thinks it is the most mainstream episode of the show.<ref name="ds interview" /> Additionally, Brooker compares it to series 3 episode "[[San Junipero]]" in that both were "a conscious decision to expand what the show was and then upend it."<ref name="RT interview" />

As a big fan of ''Star Trek'', Bridges suggested many elements from it that are incorporated in the episode, as well as borrowed concepts from the film ''[[Galaxy Quest]]'', which involved normal people suddenly pulled into an inescapable science fiction setting.<ref name="ibm">{{Cite book |last=Brooker |first=Charlie |title=Inside Black Mirror |last2=Jones |first2=Annabel |last3=Arnopp |first3=Jason |date=November 2018 |publisher=[[Crown Publishing Group]] |isbn=9781984823489 |location=New York City |chapter=USS Callister}}</ref> Brooker tells ''Den of Geek'' that the episode is not intended as an attack on ''Star Trek'', a show that was "wildly ahead of its time".<ref name="dog interview">{{Cite web |last=Mellor |first=Louisa |date=29 December 2017 |title=Black Mirror season 4: USS Callister "more homage than attack" |url=https://www.denofgeek.com/tv/black-mirror-season-4-uss-callister-more-homage-than-attack/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171229134021/http://www.denofgeek.com/uk/tv/black-mirror/53682/black-mirror-season-4-uss-callister-more-homage-than-attack |archive-date=29 December 2017 |access-date=29 December 2017 |website=Den of Geek |publisher=[[Dennis Publishing]]}}</ref> Originally, Daly's character was more unlikeable from the episode's beginning, but this was changed so that Daly strangling Walton would be more of a surprise. Brooker states that Daly dies of starvation after the events in the episode, due to the "Do Not Disturb" sign he puts on his door.<ref name="ds interview">{{Cite web |last=Jeffery |first=Morgan |date=29 December 2017 |title=Charlie Brooker breaks down Black Mirror's space saga 'USS Callister' and reveals Daly's final fate |url=http://www.digitalspy.com/tv/black-mirror/feature/a845959/black-mirror-uss-callister-ending-charlie-brooker-interview/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171229232036/http://www.digitalspy.com/tv/black-mirror/feature/a845959/black-mirror-uss-callister-ending-charlie-brooker-interview/ |archive-date=29 December 2017 |access-date=29 December 2017 |website=[[Digital Spy]]}}</ref> Haynes considered ending the episode with the shot of Daly in his apartment, rather than the happier scene of the crew playing ''Infinity'', but Brooker reassured him that not every ''Black Mirror'' episode had to end unhappily.<ref name="variety milioti">{{Cite web |last=Turchiano |first=Danielle |date=29 December 2017 |title=Cristin Milioti Breaks Down 'Black Mirror's' Stand Against a 'Misogynist Bully' in 'USS Callister' |url=https://variety.com/2017/tv/news/black-mirror-uss-callister-cristin-milioti-interview-1202640455/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171229203425/http://variety.com/2017/tv/news/black-mirror-uss-callister-cristin-milioti-interview-1202640455/ |archive-date=29 December 2017 |access-date=30 December 2017 |website=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]]}}</ref>

In the episode's initial draft, every character had a "Grain" implanted in them—a device that recorded their vision and hearing, similar to what was featured in the series one episode "[[The Entire History of You]]". This explained why virtual Nanette had the memories of real-life Nanette. Brooker decided that showing the Grain contents alongside Daly getting each person's DNA was too much detail, which led to the Grain aspect being cut. Shania says "It's a fucking gizmo" in response to a question from Nanette about how Daly's technology works, as a way to comment that the technology not making sense did not matter.<ref name="ibm" />

===Casting===
[[File:Cristin Milioti July 13, 2014 (cropped).jpg|upright|thumb|[[Cristin Milioti]] stars in the episode as Nanette Cole, who Milioti describes as a "woman in charge [fighting] against a small-minded, misogynist bully".<ref name="variety milioti" />]]
"USS ''Callister''" stars [[Jesse Plemons]] as Captain Daly and [[Cristin Milioti]] as Lieutenant Nanette, both previous stars of ''[[Fargo (TV series)|Fargo]]''. Director Toby Haynes notes that "they always wanted Jesse Plemons for the role of Daly", and that the filming dates and other cast were based around him.<ref name="THR Haynes">{{Cite web |last=Strause |first=Jackie |date=1 January 2018 |title='Black Mirror' Director on Spinoff Potential of "USS Callister" |url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/live-feed/black-mirror-uss-callister-spinoff-ideas-director-star-trek-hidden-star-wars-nods-1070875 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180102022032/https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/live-feed/black-mirror-uss-callister-spinoff-ideas-director-star-trek-hidden-star-wars-nods-1070875 |archive-date=2 January 2018 |access-date=2 January 2018 |website=[[The Hollywood Reporter]]}}</ref> Milioti accepted the role having only seen a few pages of the script; she said in an interview that Nanette is "a woman in charge [fighting] against a small-minded, misogynist bully".<ref name="variety milioti" /> [[Jimmi Simpson]], formerly known from ''[[Westworld (TV series)|Westworld]]'', and [[Michaela Coel]] of ''[[Chewing Gum (TV series)|Chewing Gum]]'' are also main characters in the episode; Coel had appeared in the previous ''Black Mirror'' episode "[[Nosedive (Black Mirror)|Nosedive]]" as an airport worker.<ref name="THR cast" /><ref>{{Cite web |last=Lutes |first=Alicia |date=5 December 2017 |title=Black Mirror's "U.S.S Callister" Trailers Gives Us An Uneasy Star Trek Adventure |url=https://archive.nerdist.com/black-mirror-uss-callister-star-trek-trailer/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171210072002/https://nerdist.com/black-mirror-uss-callister-star-trek-trailer/ |archive-date=10 December 2017 |access-date=10 December 2017 |publisher=[[Nerdist Industries]]}}</ref><ref name="Looper">{{Cite web |last=Szabo |first=Sarah |date=6 December 2017 |title=Black Mirror's 'U.S.S. Callister' revealed in spacefaring teaser |url=http://www.looper.com/99000/black-mirrors-u-s-s-callister-revealed-spacefaring-teaser/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171210004416/http://www.looper.com/99000/black-mirrors-u-s-s-callister-revealed-spacefaring-teaser/ |archive-date=10 December 2017 |access-date=10 December 2017 |website=Looper}}</ref> Simpson was ill with the flu during filming but noted that his character was intended to be skinny.<ref name="EW Simpson" /> The episode's main cast is rounded out by [[Billy Magnussen]], [[Milanka Brooks]], [[Osy Ikhile]], and Paul G. Raymond.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Feldman |first=Kate |date=9 January 2018 |title='Black Mirror's' Callister could become its own series |url=http://www.nydailynews.com/entertainment/tv/black-mirror-callister-series-article-1.3747574 |access-date=24 September 2018 |work=[[New York Daily News]]}}</ref>

[[Aaron Paul]] makes a vocal cameo appearance at the end of the episode, whilst Plemons' fiancée [[Kirsten Dunst]] makes an uncredited appearance in the office background early on, after asking the director while on set.<ref name="dunst">{{Cite web |last=Chapman |first=Tom |date=29 December 2017 |title=Black Mirror: Did You Catch USS Callister's TWO Major Cameos? |url=https://screenrant.com/black-mirror-uss-callister-aaron-paul-kirsten-dunst-cameo/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171230060231/https://screenrant.com/black-mirror-uss-callister-aaron-paul-kirsten-dunst-cameo/ |archive-date=30 December 2017 |access-date=29 December 2017 |website=Screen Rant}}</ref><ref name="THR Cameos" /> The director had to ask for the single shot she was in to be re-added after the continuity department edited it out.<ref name="THR Cameos" /> Paul's character "Gamer691" was initially supposed to be a "geeky kid", but Brooker believed that the perception of video gamers as creepy was wrong, and "he felt like it was talking down to the audience" as he is a [[gamer]] himself.<ref name="indiebts">{{Cite web |last=Miller |first=Liz Shannon |date=30 December 2017 |title='Black Mirror: USS Callister': How the Shatner Impression, Surprise Cameo, and Flawless Production Happened |url=https://www.indiewire.com/2017/12/black-mirror-uss-callister-behind-the-scenes-aaron-paul-shatner-spoilers-1201912123/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171231035738/https://www.indiewire.com/2017/12/black-mirror-uss-callister-behind-the-scenes-aaron-paul-shatner-spoilers-1201912123/ |archive-date=31 December 2017 |access-date=31 December 2017 |website=IndieWire}}</ref> He then came up with the idea that the best voice would be Paul's character [[Jesse Pinkman]] from ''[[Breaking Bad]]'', a show that featured Plemons in the role of [[Todd Alquist]].<ref name="DS Paul" />

The production approached Paul, who was a fan of ''Black Mirror'' and had already auditioned for a different episode but withdrew due to commitments with ''[[Welcome Home (2018 film)|Welcome Home]]''.<ref name="DS Paul">{{Cite web |last=Warner |first=Sam |date=25 October 2018 |title=Breaking Bad's Aaron Paul almost landed another role on Black Mirror |url=http://www.digitalspy.com/tv/black-mirror/news/a869233/black-mirror-aaron-paul-new-role-breaking-bad/ |access-date=25 October 2018 |website=[[Digital Spy]]}}</ref> Paul accepted the part on the condition that his appearance in this episode did not preclude him from being part of another ''Black Mirror'' episode.<ref name="THR Cameos">{{Cite web |last=Strause |first=Jackie |date=2 January 2018 |title='Black Mirror' Director Explains Hidden "USS Callister" Cameos |url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/live-feed/black-mirror-director-explains-aaron-paul-kirsten-dunst-uss-callister-cameos-1070949 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180102202920/https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/live-feed/black-mirror-director-explains-aaron-paul-kirsten-dunst-uss-callister-cameos-1070949 |archive-date=2 January 2018 |access-date=3 January 2018 |website=[[The Hollywood Reporter]]}}</ref><ref name="indiebts" /> He later starred in the space-themed series six episode "[[Beyond the Sea (Black Mirror)|Beyond the Sea]]".<ref>{{Cite web |last=Hamadeh |first=Yasmeen |date=15 June 2023 |title=How does Aaron Paul tie the 'Black Mirror' universe together? |url=https://mashable.com/article/black-mirror-season-6-aaron-paul-clue |access-date=16 June 2023 |website=[[Mashable]]}}</ref> The part was one of the last elements of the episode to be finished, and it surprised members of the cast when it was screened.<ref name="indiebts" />

===Filming===
Director [[Toby Haynes]] has previously worked on ''[[Sherlock (TV series)|Sherlock]]'' and ''[[Doctor Who]]'',<ref name="THR cast" /> and crew from ''Star Wars'' and 2014 film ''[[Guardians of the Galaxy (film)|Guardians of the Galaxy]]'' were hired.<ref name="ibm" /> Filming began in January 2017<ref name="ew interview" /> and ran for twenty days.<ref name="THR Haynes" /> The episode was mostly shot in the U.K., with roughly three days of filming in the [[Canary Islands]] for interplanetary scenes.<ref name="THR Haynes" /><ref name="ign" /> The scenes set on the ''Callister'' ship, Daly's apartment, and the Callister offices were shot at [[Twickenham Studios]], with all of the office scenes shot within three days.<ref name="indiebts" /> Most scenes had to be done in two or three takes, with some scenes such as Walton's description of Tommy being filmed in one take.<ref name="THR Haynes" /> Haynes and Milioti both commented on the tight schedule, with Haynes feeling that the pressure helped everyone to rise to the challenge.<ref name="indiebts" /> Brooker notes that the growth of the [[Me Too movement]] meant the episode felt more timely.<ref name="thr aug2018" />

The crew could not copy set elements directly from ''Star Trek'' without fear of legal action, but instead detailed the set in the same fashion as ''Star Trek'' or ''[[Battlestar Galactica]]''. The episode also presents ''Space Fleet'' following a similar history as ''Star Trek'', first as a 4:3 aspect ratio to represent its original broadcast format of [[Star Trek: The Original Series|the original series]], then to detailed widescreen version, and finally ending on a redesigned starship and costumes that reflect the [[J. J. Abrams]]-helmed [[Star Trek (2009 film)|reboot]].<ref name="vulturebts">{{Cite web |last=McHenry |first=Jackson |date=29 December 2017 |title=The Making of Black Mirror's Retro 'USS Callister' Episode |url=https://www.vulture.com/2017/12/black-mirror-uss-callister-star-trek-design.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171229180518/http://www.vulture.com/2017/12/black-mirror-uss-callister-star-trek-design.html |archive-date=29 December 2017 |access-date=29 December 2017 |website=[[Vulture (magazine)|Vulture]]}}</ref> Inspired by the style of 1960s television, the episode used [[Dutch angle]]s during the spaceship scenes. Cinematography towards the end was designed to evoke ''Star Trek''.<ref name="syfy">{{Cite web |last=Vineyard |first=Jennifer |date=20 August 2018 |title=Emmy Contender: Inside the Making of Black Mirror's Hit Episode 'USS Callister' |url=https://www.syfy.com/syfywire/emmy-contender-inside-the-making-of-black-mirrors-hit-episode-uss-callister |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180821010153/https://www.syfy.com/syfywire/emmy-contender-inside-the-making-of-black-mirrors-hit-episode-uss-callister |archive-date=21 August 2018 |access-date=2 September 2018 |publisher=[[Syfy Wire]]}}</ref> Haynes was a fan of ''Star Trek'', and helped to add details, such as putting Lowry in a [[redshirt (character)|red uniform]] since she was the first to be killed off. A number of ''[[Star Wars]]'' references are also included.<ref name="THR Haynes" />

The spaceship initially uses orange and red colours, and the special effects were made to look like those from the 1960s; a modern version of the ship is shown at the end of the episode, more similar to the 2009 ''[[Star Trek (2009 film)|Star Trek]]'' reboot.<ref name="ibm" /> To help the viewer distinguish between scenes set in the game and those set in the real world, Haynes had the scenes set in the game use mounted camera shots, while the real-world scenes used [[shaky camera|handheld camera]] techniques; in the scene where Daly interrupts the game to get a delivered pizza, the camera started off mounted and then switched to handheld to show the collision of those two techniques.<ref name="THR Haynes" /> Characters aboard the USS ''Callister'' wore [[neoprene]] costumes, designed to create an artificial [[Barbie]] look for the women. Daly looks like a [[Ken (doll)|Ken doll]], with his costume making him appear more muscular. Milioti aimed to change her posture and mannerisms slightly between Nanette in the real world and the virtual world. Plemons watched ''Star Trek'' and worked with a vocal coach to pay homage to [[William Shatner]]'s performance as Captain Kirk.<ref name="ibm" />

To avoid building an entire spaceship, most scenes on board the ship were set on the [[Bridge (nautical)|bridge]] or in corridors; a canteen area was considered but not used.<ref name="ibm" /> The scene where Nanette wakes up on the ship was initially going to use a medical bay, but Haynes wanted to use a circular room. The storyboard design for Lowry being turned into a monster had to be adapted during filming so the viewers could see her sprouting extra legs and tentacles. For the two planets visited in the episode, the script described one as an ''[[Indiana Jones]]''–style cave and the other as a jungle planet, but budget limitations and the filming date of February affected the choices made. The scene in which Nanette tricks Daly into swimming with her was filmed at a crater-like structure in [[Lanzarote]], using red sand from a nearby quarry, and at a lake with black sand. A drone was used to film an aerial shot of the set.<ref name="syfy" /> Both actors improvised much of the scene.<ref name="ibm" />

Production companies Painting Practice and Revolver worked on graphics and the user interfaces in the spaceship,<ref name="ibm" /> whilst special effects were done by [[Framestore]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Failes |first=Ian |date=5 July 2018 |title='Black Mirror's 'USS Callister': Crafting Effects for A Modern-Day Sci-Fi Satire |url=http://vfxvoice.com/black-mirrors-uss-callister-crafting-effects-for-a-modern-day-sci-fi-satire/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180705204128/http://vfxvoice.com/black-mirrors-uss-callister-crafting-effects-for-a-modern-day-sci-fi-satire/ |archive-date=5 July 2018 |access-date=5 July 2018 |website=VFX Voice}}</ref> Brooker says the episode features more special effects than any previous episode of the show.<ref name="dog interview" /> The Arachnajax monsters were designed to be a mixture of scary and comedic, with features like their ability to shrug making them more human-like.<ref name="ibm" /> The first cut of the episode, according to the cinematographer Stephan Pehrsson, was 90 to 95 minutes, but scenes were removed to reach the final runtime of 76 minutes.<ref>{{Cite AV media |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=FJWDprEwLKw |title='Black Mirror' Q & A with Stephan Pehrsson BSC |date=28 May 2023 |publisher=[[British Society of Cinematographers]] |via=[[YouTube]] |accessdate=11 February 2024}}</ref>{{rp|31:00–32:00}}

===Music===
British composer [[Daniel Pemberton]] composed the episode's score. A fan of ''Black Mirror'', Pemberton had worked with Brooker before on a video game magazine in the 1990s.<ref name="film music">{{Cite web |last=Schweiger |first=Daniel |date=20 December 2017 |title={{sic|Inte|view|nolink=y}} with Daniel Pemberton |url=http://www.filmmusicmag.com/?p=18378 |url-status=usurped |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180102181216/http://www.filmmusicmag.com/?p=18378 |archive-date=2 January 2018 |access-date=2 September 2018 |website=Film Music Magazine}}</ref> Pemberton was between compositions for ''[[Molly's Game]]'' and ''[[All the Money in the World]]'', but despite being busy he accepted the job for "USS ''Callister''".<ref>{{Cite web |last=Laws |first=Zach |date=20 August 2018 |title=Daniel Pemberton ('USS Callister' composer) on how he scored 'the most complicated episode' of 'Black Mirror' ever [Exclusive Video Interview] |url=https://www.goldderby.com/article/2018/daniel-pemberton-uss-callister-composer-interview-emmys-news-208693517/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180821021041/https://www.goldderby.com/article/2018/daniel-pemberton-uss-callister-composer-interview-emmys-news-208693517/ |archive-date=21 August 2018 |access-date=2 September 2018 |publisher=[[Gold Derby]]}}</ref> Pemberton says the score consisted of three styles: the ''Space Fleet'' music, the real world and Daly's video game.<ref name="variety music">{{Cite web |last=Burlingame |first=Jon |date=15 August 2018 |title=Emmys: Limited Series or TV Movie Score Nominees Range From History to Penguins |url=https://variety.com/2018/artisans/production/emmy-nominated-composers-2-1202905005/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180816113016/https://variety.com/2018/artisans/production/emmy-nominated-composers-2-1202905005/ |archive-date=16 August 2018 |access-date=2 September 2018 |website=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]]}}</ref> He also describes the soundtrack as "almost like two film scores that slowly collide".<ref name="film music" /> Pemberton wrote a score with elements reminiscent of ''Star Trek'', and other "synthetic and modern" aspects,<ref name="variety music" /> and some of the music was inspired by [[Jerry Goldsmith]].<ref name="film music" /> A 70-piece orchestra from [[Prague]] was used.<ref name="variety music" /> The soundtrack was released on [[Amazon Music]] on 29 December 2017.<ref>{{Cite web |date=28 December 2017 |title=Daniel Pemberton's Score from 'Black Mirror' Episode 'USS Callister' to Be Released |url=http://filmmusicreporter.com/2017/12/28/daniel-pembertons-score-from-black-mirror-episode-uss-callister-to-be-released/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171230223130/http://filmmusicreporter.com/2017/12/28/daniel-pembertons-score-from-black-mirror-episode-uss-callister-to-be-released/ |archive-date=30 December 2017 |access-date=2 September 2018 |website=Film Music Reporter}}</ref> A vinyl version of the soundtrack, featuring as its cover the [[Butcher Billy]]-designed ''Space Fleet'' poster seen on the episode, was released on [[Record Store Day]] 2019.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Lee, Giacomo |date=18 March 2019 |title=Butcher Billy's Black Mirror artwork for USS Callister is coming to vinyl |url=https://www.digitalartsonline.co.uk/news/illustration/butcher-billys-black-mirror-artwork-is-coming-vinyl/ |access-date=2 August 2019 |publisher=Digital Arts}}</ref>

==Analysis==
<!-- do not remove any sourced content; see talk discussion -->
[[File:Jesse Plemons (20769593584).jpg|thumb|upright|[[Jesse Plemons]] plays Robert Daly, who takes his anger out on virtual clones due to unhappiness in real life.]]
The episode is an homage to ''[[Star Trek]]''.<ref name="telegraph" /><ref name="independent" /> Using a similar set design to ''Star Trek'',<ref name="telegraph" /> the episode has been compared to another parody of the show, the 1999 film ''[[Galaxy Quest]]''.<ref name="telegraph" /><ref name="dog" /> One reviewer described "USS ''Callister''" as critical of sexism in ''Star Trek'' and its fandom,<ref name="inverse" /> with another calling it "a cruel parody and even a [[misandry|misandrous]] attack",<ref name="trekmovie" /> though Brooker says that "I don't want it to be seen that we're attacking fans of classic sci-fi".<ref name="dog interview" /> It has a similar storyline to short story "[[I Have No Mouth, and I Must Scream]]", which features characters held hostage and tortured by a supercomputer.<ref name="inverse">{{Cite web |last=Britt |first=Ryan |date=29 December 2017 |title='Black Mirror' References Sci-Fi Deeper than 'Star Trek' in "USS Callister" |url=https://www.inverse.com/article/39753-black-mirror-season-4-uss-callister-star-trek-harlan-ellison |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171230114425/https://www.inverse.com/article/39753-black-mirror-season-4-uss-callister-star-trek-harlan-ellison |archive-date=30 December 2017 |access-date=29 December 2017 |website=Inverse }}</ref> Additionally, it evokes ''[[Toy Story]]''.<ref name="dog bojalad" /> The procedurally generated game ''Infinity'' in the episode is considered to be inspired by ''[[No Man's Sky]]'', a video game released in August 2016.<ref name="verge" /> Brooker commented in October 2016 that "there's an idea for the second [Netflix] season that's sprung from a procedurally-generated universe" while playing the game.<ref>{{Cite magazine |last=Temperton |first=James |date=11 October 2016 |title=Charlie Brooker on where Black Mirror will take us next |url=https://www.wired.co.uk/article/black-mirror-technology-changing-lives |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180119235606/https://www.wired.co.uk/article/black-mirror-technology-changing-lives |archive-date=19 January 2018 |access-date=19 January 2018 |magazine=Wired}}</ref>

"USS ''Callister''" has been called "the most cinematic episode to date" for the show,<ref name="independent" /> due to its use of vivid colours and a huge fictional landscape.<ref name="dog bojalad" /><ref name="metro" /> Though the episode is dark at times and raises serious issues, it also has a perkier tone than previous ''Black Mirror'' episodes,<ref name="telegraph" /> containing [[one-line joke]]s and [[visual gag]]s,<ref name="dog" /> and a happy ending relative to other episodes of the show.<ref name="dog" /> Its plot twist is revealed slowly, a contrast to the "gut-punch" reveal of previous episodes.<ref name="metro" />

Main character Robert Daly has an unhappy life, where he does not receive credit for co-founding his company and is mocked by workplace colleagues.<ref name="independent" /> Traditionally, Daly would be the underdog character, and the story might focus on his getting revenge on Walton for stealing his credit, and for his colleagues' mistreatment of him.<ref name="EW Simpson" /> The classic plotline of a socially awkward man meeting a younger woman who appreciates his intelligence is utilised when Daly meets Nanette.<ref name="telegraph" /> As a result, viewers initially side with Daly, but instead of the pair falling in love, Daly's true nature is unmasked early.<ref name="telegraph" /> As the Captain of USS ''Callister'', he abuses his position of power, forcing his crewmates to act as opposites of themselves, such as Walton going from Daly's superior to his underling.<ref name="vulture" /> Similar to an internet bully, Daly does not seem to care about the pain he is inflicting on the virtual clones,<ref name="dog" /> treating them as action figures.<ref name="vulture" />

Critic Alec Bojalad stated that Daly fits an archetype of white males who participate in prejudiced online [[Echo chamber (media)|echo chambers]] due to social ostracisation in real life and a sense of entitlement.<ref name="dog bojalad" /> Charles Bramesco considered Daly characteristic of the nerd who assumes the role of the bully after himself being bullied.<ref name="vulture" /> [[Dana Schwartz]] linked this to the "modern toxic masculinity" movements of [[Gamergate controversy|Gamergate]] and the [[alt-right]].<ref name="EW Simpson" /> Likewise, Sonia Saraiya of ''[[Vanity Fair (magazine)|Vanity Fair]]'' called Daly an "[[Incel|incel king]]" exhibiting "a tired, stubborn form of masculinity clinging to control" with an entitlement to women compared to Nanette's [[Feminism|feminist]] fight for her own autonomy.<ref>{{Cite magazine |last=Saraiya |first=Sonia |date=12 June 2018 |title=How ''Black Mirror'' Designed an Incel King—And the Fed-Up Feminist Who Takes Him Out |url=https://www.vanityfair.com/hollywood/2018/06/black-mirror-uss-callister-jesse-plemons-cristin-milioti |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230510184928/https://www.vanityfair.com/hollywood/2018/06/black-mirror-uss-callister-jesse-plemons-cristin-milioti |archive-date=10 May 2023 |access-date=10 May 2023 |magazine=Vanity Fair }}</ref>

Charles Bramesco of ''[[Vulture (website)|Vulture]]'' noted that despite the fact that Daly never actually rapes any of the female members of the crew, he exhibits psychological traits associated with [[rape culture]].<ref name="vulture" /> Tristram Fane Saunders of ''[[The Daily Telegraph|The Telegraph]]'' called the episode "a sharp attack on an entire genre of male-driven narrative" and equates Daly's sexist fantasy involving his attractive younger co-worker with the [[Harvey Weinstein sexual abuse allegations]].<ref name="telegraph" /> Sara Moniuszko of ''[[USA Today]]'' made the same comparison, linking how Daly kisses female crew members and threatens the crew when they disobey him to Weinstein's alleged abuse.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Moniuszko |first=Sara |date=29 December 2017 |title='Black Mirror' Season 4 includes a timely episode on power dynamics and sexual harassment |url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/life/entertainthis/2017/12/29/black-mirrors-u-s-s-callister-freakishly-similar-highlights-societys-problem-power-today/974052001/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171229195856/https://www.usatoday.com/story/life/entertainthis/2017/12/29/black-mirrors-u-s-s-callister-freakishly-similar-highlights-societys-problem-power-today/974052001/ |archive-date=29 December 2017 |access-date=30 December 2017 |website=USA Today }}</ref> Brooker noted that coincidentally, news of allegations against Weinstein first broke when Brooker was on his way to a premiere of the episode in New York.<ref name="thr aug2018" /> Female crew members are dressed in sexualised outfits in Daly's game, but wear more realistic outfits when they escape.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Nicolaou |first=Elena |date=18 September 2018 |title=Black Mirror Season 4, Episode 1 Recap: "USS Callister" |url=https://www.refinery29.com/en-us/2017/12/185884/black-mirror-season-4-episode-1-uss-callister-star-trek |access-date=10 May 2023 |website=Refinery29 }}</ref>

Joho called Walton "arguably the true hero of the story", for sacrificing himself to fix the ship at the climax of the episode.<ref name="Mashable Walton" /> However, Jimmi Simpson—who played Walton—disagreed, noting that his character's thoughtlessness and selfishness were the original provocation for Daly to take revenge. Simpson opined that Walton's motive for sacrificing himself is not redemption but to "make it right for the people".<ref name="EW Simpson">{{Cite magazine |last=Schwartz |first=Dana |date=4 January 2018 |title=Jimmi Simpson has an incredibly bleak theory about his ''Black Mirror'' character's ending |url=https://ew.com/tv/2018/01/04/jimmi-simpson-black-mirror-character-theory/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180313092328/http://ew.com/tv/2018/01/04/jimmi-simpson-black-mirror-character-theory/ |archive-date=13 March 2018 |access-date=12 March 2018 |magazine=Entertainment Weekly }}</ref> Walton is absent from the ship once the characters make it into the online ''Infinity'' game; it can be interpreted that his code was deleted from Daly's modded game.<ref name="Mashable Walton">{{Cite web |last=Joho |first=Jess |date=5 January 2018 |title=The horribly bleak answer to that lingering question in 'Black Mirror' |url=https://mashable.com/2018/01/04/black-mirror-uss-callister-watson-ending-explained |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180313154544/https://mashable.com/2018/01/04/black-mirror-uss-callister-watson-ending-explained/ |archive-date=13 March 2018 |access-date=12 March 2018 |website=Mashable }}</ref> However, Simpson believed that his character remains alive, continually tortured from the pain of the incinerators.<ref name="Mashable Walton" /><ref name="EW Simpson" />

"USS Callister" features references to previous episodes of ''Black Mirror''. In addition to Brooker's remark that the episode is in some ways a successor to the third-series episode "San Junipero,"<ref name="RT interview" /> the neural implant used in this episode to transport users into the ''Infinity'' game bears the logo "TCKR", the company that developed the technology featured in that episode, the implication being that Callister Inc. uses the same software for their own games.<ref name="vulturebts" /> A reference to the second-series episode "[[White Bear (Black Mirror)|White Bear]]" is found in the names of two planets visited by the crew of Daly's virtual spaceship; the planets Skillane IV and Rannoch have been named for the criminal couple of Victoria Skillane and Iain Rannoch.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Mufson |first=Beckett |date=4 January 2018 |title=Every Easter Egg Hidden in Season Four of 'Black Mirror' |url=https://www.vice.com/en/article/every-easter-egg-in-season-four-of-black-mirror/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180305063007/https://www.vice.com/en_us/article/bjy7j8/every-easter-egg-in-season-four-of-black-mirror |archive-date=5 March 2018 |access-date=4 March 2018 |website=Vice }}</ref>

The episode has also been analysed as an on-screen rewriting of the myth of [[Don Quixote]] in the digital age, re-interpreting the figure of the Don as a monomaniacal gamer obsessed with [[space opera]] in a way comparable to the hidalgo's obsession with [[chivalric romance]]s. According to an article by Miguel Sebastián-Martín, published in [[Science Fiction Film and Television]], "USS Callister" "updates the myth for a satire of the male gamer/geek/nerd stereotype, who is reimagined as a quixotic embodiment of neoliberal, patriarchal individualism in the digital realm."<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Sebastián-Martín |first=Miguel |date=June 2022 |title=Don Quixote as gamer? |url=https://www.liverpooluniversitypress.co.uk/doi/10.3828/sfftv.2022.15 |journal=Science Fiction Film & Television |volume=15 |issue=2 |pages=193–217 |doi=10.3828/sfftv.2022.15|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

|website=[[Vulture (magazine)|Vulture]] |publisher=[[New York (magazine)|New York]]}}</ref><ref name="indiewire">{{Cite web |last=Shannon Miller |first=Liz |date=29 December 2017 |title='Black Mirror: Telegraph]]''<ref name="telegraph" /> and ''Den of Geek'',<ref name="dog bojalad" /> an A rating in [[IndieWire]],<ref name="indiewire" /> and an A− rating in ''[[The A.V. Club]]''.<ref name="avclub">{{Cite web |last=Handlen |first=Zack |date=29 December 2017 |title=''Black Mirror'' beams into a familiar nightmare as season 4 begins |url=https://www.avclub.com/black-mirror-beams-into-a-familiar-nightmare-as-season-1821633354 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180807131930/https://www.avclub.com/black-mirror-beams-into-a-familiar-nightmare-as-season-1821633354 |archive-date=7 August 2018 |access-date=10 August 2018 |website=The A.V. Club }}</ref> Cross called the episode "surely one of ''Black Mirror''{{'}}s best".<ref name="polygon">{{Cite web |last=Cross |first=Katherine |date=5 January 2018 |title=Black Mirror's 'USS Callister' filters toxic fandom through Star Trek |url=https://www.polygon.com/2018/1/5/16850656/black-mirror-season-4-uss-callister-star-trek |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180810205249/https://www.polygon.com/2018/1/5/16850656/black-mirror-season-4-uss-callister-star-trek |archive-date=10 August 2018 |access-date=10 August 2018 |website=[[Polygon (website)|Polygon]]}}</ref> Saunders thought that the male abuse of power is "prescient" and "topical",<ref name="telegraph" /> while Bojalad wrote that the episode's timing is "just right".<ref name="dog bojalad" /> However, Dileo criticised the episode as "possibly not the deepest or most insightful" of the programme,<ref name="ign" /> and Oller wrote that the episode's "mixed metaphors" cause positive aspects to be "drowned out".<ref name="paste" />

The episode's parody of ''Star Trek'' has been widely praised,<ref name="vulture" /><ref name="dog">{{Cite web |last=Lambie |first=Ryan |date=29 December 2017 |title=Black Mirror season 4: USS Callister review |url=https://www.denofgeek.com/tv/black-mirror-season-4-uss-callister-review/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180131234846/http://www.denofgeek.com/uk/tv/black-mirror/54116/black-mirror-season-4-uss-callister-review |archive-date=31 January 2018 |access-date=10 August 2018 |website=Den of Geek }}</ref> with Statt calling it an "unabashed love letter to ''Star Trek''",<ref name="verge">{{Cite web |last=Statt |first=Nick |date=2 January 2018 |title=In Black Mirror's USS Callister, the true villains are real-world tech moguls |url=https://www.theverge.com/2018/1/2/16841938/black-mirror-uss-callister-review-netflix-season-4-jesse-plemons-cristin-milioti |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180807230532/https://www.theverge.com/2018/1/2/16841938/black-mirror-uss-callister-review-netflix-season-4-jesse-plemons-cristin-milioti |archive-date=7 August 2018 |access-date=10 August 2018 |website=The Verge }}</ref> while Franich described it as a "knowing parody" and "loving hyperbolization".<ref name="ew" /> Cross believes it has a "love for the source material".<ref name="polygon" /> Statt also praised the episode's references to other media such as ''No Man's Sky''.<ref name="verge" /> However, it has also received criticism. Lambie wrote that allusions to ''Star Trek'' "aren't all that new",<ref name="dog" /> while Saunders believed that the numerous references "clobber you over the head".<ref name="telegraph">{{Cite news |last=Saunders |first=Tristram Fane |date=29 December 2017 |title=Black Mirror, season 4, USS Callister, review: a sharp, topical attack on an entire genre of male-driven narrative |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/on-demand/0/black-mirror-season-4-uss-callister-review-sharp-topical-attack/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180630224748/https://www.telegraph.co.uk/on-demand/0/black-mirror-season-4-uss-callister-review-sharp-topical-attack/ |archive-date=30 June 2018 |access-date=10 August 2018 |work=The Telegraph }}</ref> Oller called them "heavy-handed", believing they overshadow the episode's message.<ref name="paste">{{Cite web |last=Oller |first=Jacob |date=29 December 2017 |title=''Black Mirror'' Review: The Muddled "USS Callister" Opens Season Four on a Low Note |url=https://www.pastemagazine.com/articles/2017/12/black-mirror-review-uss-callister.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180810205732/https://www.pastemagazine.com/articles/2017/12/black-mirror-review-uss-callister.html |archive-date=10 August 2018 |access-date=10 August 2018 |website=Paste }}</ref> In a negative review, Whitley opined that although the episode has the right number of references, they are used in a "cruel parody and even a [[Misandry|misandrous]] attack on male science-fiction fans".<ref name="trekmovie">{{Cite web |last=Whitley |first=Jared |date=29 December 2017 |title=REVIEW: Black Mirror's "USS Callister" Ain't No 'Galaxy Quest' |url=https://trekmovie.com/2017/12/29/review-black-mirrors-uss-callister-aint-no-galaxy-quest/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180813072825/https://trekmovie.com/2017/12/29/review-black-mirrors-uss-callister-aint-no-galaxy-quest/ |archive-date=13 August 2018 |access-date=10 August 2018 |website=Trek Movie }}</ref>

"USS ''Callister''" is more comedic than previous episodes of ''Black Mirror'' and explores a genre which is new for the show, both of which were well received.<ref name="ign">{{Cite web |last=Dileo |first=Adam |date=6 October 2017 |title=Black Mirror: Season 4 Christmas Episode "USS Callister" Premiere Impressions |url=https://uk.ign.com/articles/2017/10/07/black-mirror-season-4-christmas-episode-premiere-impressions |access-date=10 August 2018 |website=IGN }}</ref> Statt described it as "laugh-out-loud funny";<ref name="verge" /> Sims called it "darkly funny";<ref name="atlantic">{{Cite web |last=Sims |first=David |date=29 December 2017 |title=''Black Mirror''{{'}}s 'USS Callister' Is Much More Than a ''Star Trek'' Parody |url=https://www.theatlantic.com/entertainment/archive/2017/12/black-mirrors-uss-callister-is-much-more-than-a-star-trek-parody/549191/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180810205730/https://www.theatlantic.com/entertainment/archive/2017/12/black-mirrors-uss-callister-is-much-more-than-a-star-trek-parody/549191/ |archive-date=10 August 2018 |access-date=10 August 2018 |website=The Atlantic }}</ref> and, in a negative review, Oller wrote that the "comedy is far better than the actual story".<ref name="paste" /> Stolworthy calls the genre change "heaps of fun",<ref name="independent">{{Cite web |last=Stolworthy |first=Jacob |date=29 December 2017 |title=Black Mirror season 4 episode 1 'USS Callister' spoiler review: Space romp is worthy of a spinoff if future ideas dry up |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/arts-entertainment/tv/reviews/black-mirror-season-4-episode-1-uss-callister-netflix-review-spoiler-jesse-plemons-cristin-milotti-a8131296.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180630054339/https://www.independent.co.uk/arts-entertainment/tv/reviews/black-mirror-season-4-episode-1-uss-callister-netflix-review-spoiler-jesse-plemons-cristin-milotti-a8131296.html |archive-date=30 June 2018 |access-date=10 August 2018 |website=The Independent }}</ref> while Statt called it "refreshingly different".<ref name="verge" /> Starkey described the episode as proof that the show has room to grow.<ref name="metro">{{Cite web |last=Starkey |first=Adam |date=29 December 2017 |title=Black Mirror season 4 spoiler review: USS Callister is a spectacular cinematic leap |url=http://metro.co.uk/2017/12/29/black-mirror-season-4-spoiler-review-uss-callister-is-a-spectacular-new-direction-7189242/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180618105929/https://metro.co.uk/2017/12/29/black-mirror-season-4-spoiler-review-uss-callister-is-a-spectacular-new-direction-7189242/ |archive-date=18 June 2018 |access-date=10 August 2018 |website=Metro }}</ref>

The ending and DNA cloning technology have both been highlighted by critics, garnering mixed reception. Saunders said the episode's ending "might not feel very Black Mirror" but is "the kind of story it would be good to hear more often".<ref name="telegraph" /> Starkey described the ending as "wonderfully bleak",<ref name="metro" /> while Sims praised the happy ending.<ref name="atlantic" /> However, Handlen called it "sudden" and "rushed", believing that the episode is "a little too eager to please", which causes it to lose tension.<ref name="avclub" /> Oller lambasted the episode for numerous plot holes and its "sprawling sci-fi rules and nonsense" such as the DNA cloning plot device.<ref name="paste" /> VanDerWerff similarly criticised the cloning technology's lack of explanation;<ref name="vox">{{Cite web |last=VanDerWerff |first=Emily |date=29 December 2017 |title=Black Mirror's "USS Callister" turns white guy nerd fantasies into a terrifying trap |url=https://www.vox.com/culture/2017/12/29/16804664/black-mirror-uss-callister-recap-season-4-review |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180810205322/https://www.vox.com/culture/2017/12/29/16804664/black-mirror-uss-callister-recap-season-4-review |archive-date=10 August 2018 |access-date=6 October 2019 |website=Vox }}</ref> Handlen called it "magic that you either go with or you don't".<ref name="avclub" />

Other parts of the plot have also received mixed reception. Starkey believed the "early plot jumps" are "slightly heavy-handed".<ref name="metro" /> Sims praised the twist which reveals that Daly is not the protagonist.<ref name="atlantic" /> Lambie opined that the flashback with Walton's son adds a "chill running through the middle of the episode",<ref name="dog" /> but VanDerWerff criticised that it unnecessarily adds length to the episode.<ref name="vox" /> VanDerWerff compared the crew's escape plan favourably to a "movie prison break",<ref name="vox" /> though Franich believed that the fast pace causes the "dull" blackmail of Nanette to be "a too-easy gag".<ref name="ew" /> Stolworthy said the length of the episode is justified,<ref name="independent" /> though Starkey wrote that the episode "occasionally meanders",<ref name="metro" /> and Sims concurred that the episode is "a mite too long".<ref name="atlantic" />

The cast of the episode have been widely praised.<ref name="ign" /><ref name="paste" /> Saunders wrote that Plemons is "obviously perfect" as Daly,<ref name="dog bojalad" /> and he was praised by Lambie, Miller and Franich for his acting of Daly's two different personalities.<ref name="dog" /><ref name="indiewire" /><ref name="ew" /> VanDerWerff wrote that Plemons "blends a surprisingly great [[William Shatner]] riff with a slow-building sense of odiousness".<ref name="vox" /> Miller called the character "truly grounded in reality" due to the writing and acting.<ref name="indiewire" /> Simpson's performance as Walton is singled out by Stolworthy and Bojalad for praise,<ref name="independent" /><ref name="dog bojalad" /> with Starkey describing him as the episode's "emotional centerpiece".<ref name="metro" /> Bojalad called Milioti's character Nanette the "real revelation" of the episode,<ref name="dog bojalad" /> while Cross stated that she was "painfully easy" to relate to.<ref name="polygon" /> Darren Franich of ''[[Entertainment Weekly]]'' called for Milioti to receive an [[Emmy Awards|Emmy]] nomination for Best Actress for her performance as Nanette in the episode.<ref>{{Cite magazine |last=Franich |first=Darren |date=1 June 2018 |title=Early Emmy Plea: Black Mirror's Cristin Milioti reinvented sci-fi heroism in 'U.S.S. Callister' |url=https://ew.com/tv/2018/06/01/black-mirror-emmy-cristin-milioti-callister/ |access-date=10 May 2023 |magazine=Entertainment Weekly }}</ref> Stolworthy wrote that Coel's performance as Lowry stands out.<ref name="independent" /> However, VanDerWerff criticised that the episode's minor characters are "mostly quick sketches".<ref name="vox" />

"USS ''Callister''" has been described as the show's "most cinematic episode to date",<ref name="independent" /> and the episode with "by far the highest production values".<ref name="ign" /> Bojalad praised the "bright, beautiful pastel color",<ref name="dog bojalad" /> while Dileo noted the "jaw-dropping special effects".<ref name="ign" /> Statt called the episode "visually stunning", concluding it is "the first episode of ''Black Mirror'' that feels like it belongs in a movie theater".<ref name="verge" /> Franich wrote that the cinematography "captures the effect" of the original ''Star Trek''.<ref name="ew" />

* 7th – Corey Atad, ''[[Esquire (magazine)|Esquire]]''<ref name="esquire ranking">{{Cite web |last=Atad, Corey |date=24 October 2016 |title=Every Episode of Black Mirror, Ranked |url=http://www.esquire.com/entertainment/tv/a49919/black-mirror-episodes-ranked/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170815171949/http://www.esquire.com/entertainment/tv/a49919/black-mirror-episodes-ranked/ |archive-date=15 August 2017 |access-date=21 June 2020 |website=[[Esquire (magazine)|Esquire]] |publisher=[[Hearst Communications]]}}</ref>
* 8th – Morgan Jeffery, ''[[Digital Spy]]''<ref name="ds ranking">{{Cite web |last=Jeffery |first=Morgan |date=9 April 2017 |title=Ranking all 13 episodes of Charlie Brooker's chilling Black Mirror |url=http://www.digitalspy.com/tv/black-mirror/feature/a780434/black-mirror-episodes-ranked-charlie-brooker/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180806110935/http://www.digitalspy.com/tv/black-mirror/feature/a780434/black-mirror-episodes-ranked-charlie-brooker/ |archive-date=6 August 2018 |access-date=10 August 2018 |website=[[Digital Spy]]}}</ref>

==Sequel==
After its release, Brooker and Jones said "USS ''Callister''" would be the episode most suited to a sequel. Brooker said the final scene leaves the characters "in a universe of infinite possibilities" with "a lot of question marks".<ref name="thr aug2018" /> Haynes suggested it would work as a television series and that he would be interested in working on it. He speculated that Daly was left in a coma and his attempted murder would be investigated.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Ling |first=Thomas |date=2 January 2018 |title=Black Mirror director says he wants to do a spin-off of USS Callister |url=https://www.radiotimes.com/tv/sci-fi/black-mirror-director-says-he-wants-to-do-a-spin-off-of-uss-callister/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210624203203/https://www.radiotimes.com/tv/sci-fi/black-mirror-director-says-he-wants-to-do-a-spin-off-of-uss-callister/ |archive-date=24 June 2021 |access-date=18 June 2021 |website=[[Radio Times]]}}</ref> The series was about to enter development in 2023 when it was derailed by the [[2023 SAG-AFTRA strike]], and the ideas pitched for the series were reworked into a single [[television film]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Strause|first=Jackie|date=14 April 2025|title='Black Mirror' Sequel "USS Callister: Into Infinity" Was Initially a Series. Now It May Be a Trilogy|url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/tv/tv-features/black-mirror-uss-callister-into-infinity-sequel-tv-series-trilogy-1236190152/|website=[[Hollywood Reporter]]}}</ref>

In March 2024, Netflix announced that a sequel, titled "[[USS Callister: Into Infinity|USS ''Callister''{{hairsp}}: Into Infinity]]",<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |last=Strause |first=Jackie |date=31 March 2025 |title='Black Mirror' Season 7 Trailer and Episodic Details Revealed |url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/tv/tv-news/black-mirror-season-7-trailer-episode-details-1236176503/ |access-date=31 March 2025 |website=[[The Hollywood Reporter]] }}</ref> would air as part of the seventh series in 2025, marking the first ''Black Mirror'' story to receive a continuation. Alongside a 30-second announcement trailer, a spokesperson said: "Robert Daly is dead, but for the crew of the USS ''Callister'', their problems are just beginning".<ref>{{Cite web |last=Szalai |first=George |date=14 March 2024 |title='Black Mirror' Season 7 to Hit Netflix in 2025, Including 'USS Callister' Sequel |url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/tv/tv-news/netflix-black-mirror-season-7-2025-uss-callister-1235851460/ |access-date=17 March 2024 |website=[[The Hollywood Reporter]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Craig |first=David |date=15 March 2024 |title=Black Mirror confirms season 7 for 2025 – including sequel episode |url=https://www.radiotimes.com/tv/sci-fi/black-mirror-season-7-confirmed-2025-newsupdate/ |access-date=17 March 2024 |website=[[Radio Times]]}}</ref> With a runtime of 88 minutes, it is the second longest ''Black Mirror'' episode after "[[Hated in the Nation]]".<ref name=":0" /><ref name="Collider">{{Cite web |last=Chitwood |first=Adam |date=21 October 2016 |title='Black Mirror' Season 3 Review: The Future Is Slightly Sunnier on Netflix |url=https://collider.com/black-mirror-season-3-review/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161005121413/http://collider.com/black-mirror-season-3-review/ |archive-date=5 October 2016 |access-date=26 December 2020 |website=[[Collider (website)|Collider]]}}</ref>
